question: Should we build our own customer-support ticketing system or buy an off-the-shelf one?
context: Q3 planning. A 'build' commits the two available senior engineers for the quarter; a 'buy' commits to an annual contract and a first-time vendor security review.

evidence.statement: Support runs on shared email inboxes today; volume is about 400 tickets/week and growing roughly 8% per quarter.
Two senior backend engineers are free for a Q3 project; their fully-loaded cost is about $95k for the quarter.
The leading off-the-shelf vendor quoted $1,900/month for the team's seat count on an annual contract.
Four internal systems (billing, inventory, CRM, provisioning) hold data that support agents currently copy between by hand.
The vendor's API allows custom integrations, but each non-standard connector is quoted as a separate paid professional-services engagement.
The last internal tool build (a reporting dashboard) shipped 5 months late and still needs about 1 day/week of maintenance.
CSAT is 78%; the dominant complaint theme is slow first-response time.
No one on the team has run a security or procurement review for an external SaaS vendor that would handle customer data.
